when.field: The receiver of .name or ?.name is not null and not a map. name is the field word; kind is the receiver's kind
when.index: The receiver of [e] or ?.[e] is not null, and not a list, a string or a map. kind is the receiver's kind
when.method: In the shape test of a method call whose method is found at run time, first: the receiver is not null and its kind has no method of that name. Raised before the arguments are evaluated. kind is the receiver's kind; name is the method's name
when.operands: A binary operator is given two operands, neither null, whose kinds do not go together. op is the operator's canonical text, such as not in with one space; left and right are the kinds of the two operands
when.operand: A unary operator is given an operand of a kind it does not take. op is the operator's canonical text; kind is the operand's kind
when.whole: A list or string index or an exponent is not a whole number, or an index on a list or string is not a number; or an argument of the right kind for a library parameter of type int is a number that is not whole. found is that value
when.key: A computed key, the key in [k] on a map, or the key field of an element of toMap, is not a string. found is that value
when.spread-list: A spread in a list literal is given a value that is not null and not a list. kind is its kind
when.spread-map: A spread in a map literal is given a value that is not null and not a map. kind is its kind
when.pattern-list: A list pattern is matched against a value that is not null and not a list. kind is its kind
when.pattern-map: A map pattern is matched against a value that is not null and not a map. kind is its kind
when.text: An opaque value is rendered as text, at any depth: in a template, or by string
when.json: An opaque value is written as JSON
when.argument: An argument of a library function or method is of a kind its parameter does not accept, null included, and the parameter is not bound ordered. The receiver is tested first, then each argument left to right; for one argument the test of kind comes before the test for a whole number, so fixed("a", 2.5) takes this template. name is the entry's name as written in the program; kind is the argument's kind
when.count: In the shape test of a method call whose method is found at run time, after method: the method does not accept that count of arguments. name is the method's name; count is the count of arguments written
when.unordered: A library entry needs an ordered set (the arguments of min and max, the elements of min, max, sort and unique, the keys sortBy's callback gave), and the set is not all numbers or all strings. Every failure of kind at a parameter or element bound ordered takes this template, null and a list included. The scan stops at the first value that fails: the first that is neither a number nor a string, or the first whose kind differs from the first value's, whichever comes first. name is the entry's name; kind is the kind of that value
when.element: A library entry tests the elements of its receiver and one is of a kind it does not take, null included: sum, flat, join, and an element of toMap that is not a map. name is the entry's name; kind is the kind of the first such element
when.result: A library entry tests each result of its callback and one is of a kind it does not take, null included: flatMap and groupBy. name is the entry's name; kind is that result's kind
when.callback: In the shape test of a method call whose method is found at run time, an argument at a callback parameter is not a lambda written in place or the name of a const-bound lambda. Tested with not-callback in one pass, left to right, after method and count. count is the argument's position, from 1, not counting the receiver; name is the method's name
when.not-callback: In the same pass as callback, an argument at a parameter that is not a callback is a lambda. For an opaque receiver every lambda argument fails this test. count is the argument's position, from 1, not counting the receiver; name is the method's name
when.parameters: In a second pass, left to right, after callback and not-callback, a lambda argument declares more parameters than the entry calls it with. name is the method's name; count is the number of arguments the entry calls the lambda with
